  "title": "Choose first federal data source",
  "body": "A few considerations when choosing the first federal data source to connect to:\r\n\r\n__1. Which states use it?__\r\n\r\nWe know that all states must consult the Social Security Administration's Death Master File, the National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES), the List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE), the Excluded Parties List System (EPLS) (see [CFR 42](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/455.436)).  I believe all states also consult [PECOS](https://pecos.cms.hhs.gov/pecos/login.do#headingLv1), but see [this GAO report](https://www.gao.gov/products/GAO-16-402) on the wide variety of databases that states and managed care plans consult when screening providers.\r\n\r\n__2. How crucial is it to the function of the PSM?__\r\n\r\nEPLS and PECOS both show up in many places in the codebase (245 instances of EPLS and 199 instances of PECOS), while NPPES and LEIE only appear in the documentation.  So, likely EPLS and PECOS would be preferred for this one.\r\n\r\n__3. What steps do we need to take to use data from it?  Does it have an API or standard ETL process?__\r\n\r\nEPLS data is available in a public extract [here](https://www.sam.gov/portal/SAM/?navigationalstate=JBPNS_rO0ABXdcACJqYXZheC5mYWNlcy5wb3J0bGV0YnJpZGdlLlNUQVRFX0lEAAAAAQApdmlldzpiOWYzY2M4Yi1hZWZmLTRkMmQtOWU0MC01YzkxZTg0MjAyNTYAB19fRU9GX18*&portal:componentId=24f38525-a064-4a77-b09f-3fa5986c2b48&interactionstate=JBPNS_rO0ABXc0ABBfanNmQnJpZGdlVmlld0lkAAAAAQATL2pzZi9uYXZpZ2F0aW9uLmpzcAAHX19FT0ZfXw**&portal:type=action##11), but there are restrictions on access: \r\n\r\n>Systematic access (electronic harvesting) or extraction of content from the website, including the use of \"bots\" or \"spiders\", is prohibited.\r\n\r\nPECOS doesn't have an API yet, and at least some states still do manual lookups.  A monthly extract may be available.\r\n\r\n\r\n",

      "id": 302464845,

      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "My chat with @brainwane reminded me I wasn't updating this issue.  So: after some discussion, @cecilia-donnelly and I settled on DMF and EPLS as our first targets.\r\n\r\n[Per HHS's OIG](https://oig.hhs.gov/faqs/exclusions-faq.asp), it looks like EPLS is a superset of LEIE:\r\n\r\n    What is the difference between the LEIE and the General Services\r\n    Administration's (GSA) Excluded Parties List System (EPLS) and\r\n    System for Award Management (SAM) websites?\r\n\r\n    GSA administers EPLS and SAM, both of which contain debarment\r\n    actions taken by various Federal agencies, including exclusion\r\n    actions taken by the OIG. The List of Excluded\r\n    Individuals/Entities contains only the exclusion actions taken by\r\n    the OIG. You may access the EPLS at: http://www.epls.gov External\r\n    link and SAM at https://www.sam.gov External link.\r\n\r\n@brainwane, can you confirm that EPLS is a superset of LEIE? Thanks!"
    },
    {
      "id": 302529071,
      "url": "https://github.com/SolutionGuidance/psm/issues/17#issuecomment-302529071",
      "created_at": "2017-05-18T20:17:11Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "Some questions to ask about these federal data sources (for @brainwane and everyone): \r\n\r\n   - Do they have dev/test versions that we could use while in development?  (A sample data file or test API, perhaps.)\r\n   - What are their gating mechanisms?  Can we easily use their authorization checks?  That is, do we need to set up some authorization system for states or can we use one that's already built into the data source?\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 302537286,
      "url": "https://github.com/SolutionGuidance/psm/issues/17#issuecomment-302537286",
      "created_at": "2017-05-18T20:50:14Z",

      "body": "@jvasile I'm researching to double-check that question right now."
    },
    {
      "id": 302736906,
      "url": "https://github.com/SolutionGuidance/psm/issues/17#issuecomment-302736906",
      "created_at": "2017-05-19T15:38:11Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "Some more background on SAM/EPLS/LEIE: http://blog.providertrust.com/blog/OIG-LEIE-vs-SAM.gov-OMG"

      "id": 303156837,
      "url": "https://github.com/SolutionGuidance/psm/issues/17#issuecomment-303156837",

      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "Subscription options and sample code for accessing the Death Master File are available [here](https://www.ssdmf.com/FolderID/97/SessionID/%7B43FD1DB0-2F5B-4539-A5CE-149B675B6764%7D/PageVars/Library/InfoManage/Guide.htm).  "
    },
    {
      "id": 303171466,
      "url": "https://github.com/SolutionGuidance/psm/issues/17#issuecomment-303171466",
      "created_at": "2017-05-22T17:46:41Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "CSV download for LEIE: https://oig.hhs.gov/exclusions/exclusions_list.asp"
    },
    {
      "id": 303942592,
      "url": "https://github.com/SolutionGuidance/psm/issues/17#issuecomment-303942592",
      "created_at": "2017-05-25T07:22:27Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "For the Death Master File, there does not seem to be an official source of sample data, but http://ssdmf.info/ provides a downloadable sample from 30 November 2011.\r\n\r\nThe schema of the ssdmf.info file does not entirely match the schema presented in https://dmf.ntis.gov/recordlayout.pdf . But the sample file has a consistent layout. Differences:\r\n\r\n* \"name suffix\" is very rarely present, and the fieldsize/position is off by one: 30-33 instead of 31-34.\r\n* The middle name does not have a multi-character field, but a middle *initial* (a single character) is present."
    },
    {
      "id": 303945040,
      "url": "https://github.com/SolutionGuidance/psm/issues/17#issuecomment-303945040",
      "created_at": "2017-05-25T07:37:25Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "As @cecilia-donnelly noted, CSV download for LEIE is at https://oig.hhs.gov/exclusions/exclusions_list.asp ; the April download is at https://oig.hhs.gov/exclusions/downloadables/UPDATED.csv . It seems to be updated monthly. My visual inspection of the April download shows that it's consonant with the schema as described in https://oig.hhs.gov/exclusions/files/leie_record_layout.pdf ."
    },
    {
      "id": 304133699,
      "url": "https://github.com/SolutionGuidance/psm/issues/17#issuecomment-304133699",
      "created_at": "2017-05-25T21:47:07Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "@brainwane, what about the 2013 ssdmf sample?  Does it match the modern dmf schema?"
    },
    {
      "id": 304210120,
      "url": "https://github.com/SolutionGuidance/psm/issues/17#issuecomment-304210120",
      "created_at": "2017-05-26T07:12:43Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "@jvasile The 2013 ssdmf sample (as found at http://cancelthesefunerals.com/ ) is -- from a visual inspection -- consistent with the 2011 sample. That is to say:\r\n\r\n* it also has a middle *initial* field rather than a multi-character field for a middle name\r\n* the fieldsize/position for \"name suffix\" is off (30-33 instead of 31-34 -- also, sometimes, the name suffix is immediately following the \"Last Name\", e.g., HARIHARESWARA JR with only a single space in between)"
    },
    {
      "id": 305660346,
      "url": "https://github.com/SolutionGuidance/psm/issues/17#issuecomment-305660346",
      "created_at": "2017-06-02T00:58:18Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "I'm going to close this.  We've chosen a first ETL target, which is LEIE.  We have real data and it has a simple ETL process attached to it.  There is other data source work to do, but we've met the goal of this issue.  Thanks, all!"
    }
